page: CSRF Protection Middleware protecting against cross-site request forgery by validating Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site headers. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {csrf} from 'hono/csrf'. HTTP headers: Origin, Sec-Fetch-Site (Fetch Metadata). Validates only unsafe HTTP methods (not GET, HEAD, OPTIONS). Content-Types validated: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data, text/plain. Request allowed if Origin validation OR Sec-Fetch-Site validation passes (either sufficient). Default behavior: same-origin only. Sec-Fetch-Site standard values: same-origin (same origin), same-site (same site different subdomain), cross-site (different site), none (not from web page like address bar). Options: origin (string | string[] | (origin: string, context: Context) => boolean, default same-origin), secFetchSite (string | string[] | (secFetchSite: string, context: Context) => boolean, default 'same-origin'). Security: verify protocol with $, never forward match with regex. Caveats: old browsers without Origin headers, reverse proxies removing headers - use token methods instead. Use case: webhook endpoints allow cross-site, standard endpoints same-origin. Questions: How to protect against CSRF? Which headers are checked? Can I allow multiple origins? sections.manifest: Import statements for CSRF middleware. import {Hono} from 'hono' for the main framework class. import {csrf} from 'hono/csrf' for the middleware function. Questions: What to import? Where is csrf located?

CSRF protection usage patterns. Pattern 1: Default CSRF protection. app.use(csrf()). Validates Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site headers. Pattern 2: Allow single origin. csrf({origin: 'https://myapp.example.com'}). Pattern 3: Allow multiple origins. csrf({origin: ['https://myapp.example.com', 'https://development.myapp.example.com']}). Pattern 4: Single Sec-Fetch-Site value. csrf({secFetchSite: 'same-origin'}). Pattern 5: Multiple Sec-Fetch-Site values. csrf({secFetchSite: ['same-origin', 'none']}). Pattern 6: Dynamic origin validation. csrf({origin: (origin) => /https:\/\/(\w+\.)?myapp\.example\.com$/.test(origin)}). Security: use $ to ensure exact end match, never forward match. Pattern 7: Dynamic Sec-Fetch-Site validation. csrf({secFetchSite: (secFetchSite, c) => secFetchSite === 'same-origin' || (secFetchSite === 'cross-site' && c.req.path.startsWith('/webhook/'))}). Can access c.req.path for dynamic rules. Questions: How to enable CSRF protection? How to allow origins? Can I use regex? How to allow webhooks? Can I make validation dynamic? CSRF middleware options specification. Optional: origin (string | string[] | (origin: string, context: Context) => boolean, default same-origin). String: single allowed origin like 'https://example.com'. Array: multiple allowed origins. Function: custom validation, receives Origin header value and Context, enables dynamic validation based on request properties. Default: only same origin. Function receives request Origin and context for flexibility. Security: always verify protocol and use exact match ($), never forward match. Optional: secFetchSite (string | string[] | (secFetchSite: string, context: Context) => boolean, default 'same-origin'). String: single value like 'same-origin'. Array: multiple values like ['same-origin', 'none']. Function: custom validation, receives Sec-Fetch-Site header value and Context. Default: only 'same-origin'. Standard values: same-origin (same origin), same-site (same site different subdomain), cross-site (different site), none (not from web page like address bar). Questions: Which options are required?
